title: Authy Desktop Is Gone. What to Use on a Mac Instead
meta_title: Authy Desktop Alternative for Mac. What to Use Instead.
description: Authy Desktop for Mac ended on 19 March 2024 and Authy has no export. Here is what still works, which Mac apps replace it and how to move safely.
card: Authy Desktop ended in March 2024. What a Mac user can do now, and what leaving Authy really costs.
lede: Authy Desktop for Mac reached its end of life on 19 March 2024, and Twilio no longer updates it. To get codes for two factor authentication, or 2FA, on a Mac you now need a different app. Authy has no export, so you move by setting up 2FA again at each service, one at a time, while Authy still works on your phone.

sections.html:
Twilio, the company that makes Authy, announced the change in its changelog on 19 February 2024. The Authy Desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux would reach their end of life on 19 March 2024. The same entry says the date had been August 2024 and was brought forward.

The Authy system requirements page now lists the apps for Linux, Mac and Windows computers as deprecated, and says Twilio does not update them any more. The platforms it lists as officially supported are Android, iPhone and iPad.

If you find an Authy Desktop installer on a download site, leave it alone. The same Twilio page names the Apple App Store and the Google Play Store as the places to get Authy, and a desktop installer from anywhere else is software its maker has stopped updating.

sections.h2: Can You Still Use Authy on a Mac?
sections.html:
Not in any way Twilio supports. Its system requirements page lists the Mac only under deprecated items, and it says that a device missing from the supported list is not officially supported and may have usability problems.

If the App Store on your Mac offers you Authy, the same warning applies. The Mac is not on the supported list, so Twilio does not promise that Authy will work there or keep working.

What does still work is Authy on your phone. You can keep it there and type each 2FA code into your Mac by hand. If that is enough for you, there is nothing to move. If you want your 2FA codes on the Mac itself, you need another app.

No. A Twilio help page, checked on 19 November 2026, says the Authy app does not allow importing or exporting 2FA account tokens, and gives security as the reason.

The route Twilio gives instead is to sign in to each service, turn 2FA off, turn it on again, and scan the new QR code with the app you are moving to.

That page gives no other route. Be wary of any script or tool that claims to pull the keys out of Authy. Running unknown software against the keys to all your sign ins is a risk in itself.

So the real cost of leaving Authy is time. There is no bulk move. Each service has to be visited once, and a service run by your employer may need your IT team to reset 2FA for you.

sections.h2: How to Move From Authy to a Mac App, One Account at a Time
sections.html:
Read this before you start. Do not delete Authy from your phone, remove a token inside Authy, or delete your Authy account until every service works with the new app. Twilio warns that if you delete your Authy account while a service still has its 2FA tied to Authy, you may be unable to sign in to that service.

  1. Install the new app on your Mac and open it once, so you know it runs.
  2. Choose one service. Sign in to it on your Mac, using the 2FA code from Authy on your phone.
  3. Open the security settings of that service and find 2FA, which some services call two step verification. Some let you change the authenticator app directly. Otherwise turn 2FA off, then turn it on again straight away.
  4. The service shows a QR code, and usually a setup key in letters and numbers as well. Add it to the new app. A Mac app cannot point a camera at its own screen, so use a screenshot of the QR code if your app reads images, or copy the setup key.
  5. Type the 2FA code from the new app into the service to finish.
  6. If the service gives you new recovery codes, save them somewhere safe. The old ones may no longer work.
  7. Sign out and sign in again with a 2FA code from the new app. When that works, this service is done.
  8. Go on to the next service. Start with your email, since other services send their reset links there.

Leave 2FA off only for as long as the change takes. Finish each service before you start another.

When every service works from the new app, you can remove Authy. Twilio says deleting an Authy account runs over a 30 day period with confirmation emails, and cannot be reversed once it completes.

sections.h2: Which Mac App Should Replace Authy?
sections.html:
Authy users were used to the same 2FA codes on a computer and a phone, so look for an app that has a real Mac version and keeps your devices in step.

  • Apple Passwords is part of macOS Sequoia 15 and later, so there is nothing to install. The guide linked below has its steps.
  • Ente Auth lists apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android. Its makers describe it as free and open source, with end to end encrypted sync.
  • Proton Authenticator lists apps for Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad and Android. Proton says it is free on all of them, with end to end encrypted sync if you sign in with a Proton Account.

None of these gives you a shortcut out of Authy. The apps Proton names for import, for example, do not include Authy.

AuthSome is our own app, coming soon to the App Store. It is a free native app for iPhone, iPad and Mac, with a menu bar panel on the Mac and end to end encrypted iCloud sync between your Apple devices. It does not import from Authy either, so the steps above apply to it as well. It needs macOS 26 or later, and it has no Android or Windows version. If you use either of those, choose one of the apps that does.

For the setup steps in Passwords and a wider look at the choices, read Can You Use an Authenticator App on a Mac? For how keeping two devices in step works, read Can You Use the Same Authenticator App on Two Devices? If cost is your worry, see which authenticator apps are free with no ads or subscription.

faq.q: Is Authy Desktop Still Available to Download?
faq.a: Not from Twilio. Its help pages list only the iPhone, iPad and Android apps as supported, and name the App Store and Google Play as the places to get them. Copies on other download sites are the ended desktop app.

faq.q: Can You Import Authy Into Another Authenticator App?
faq.a: No. Twilio says Authy does not allow exporting tokens, so another app has nothing to read. Each service has to be set up again with a new QR code.

faq.q: What Happens If You Delete Authy Before Moving Your Accounts?
faq.a: You may be locked out of every service that still expects an Authy 2FA code. Your way back in is the recovery codes each service gave you, or its own support team.

faq.q: What Is a Good Authy Alternative on iPhone as Well as Mac?
faq.a: Pick one app that runs on both and syncs between them, so you set up each service once. Apple Passwords, Ente Auth and Proton Authenticator all have iPhone and Mac apps.
